from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Music relies on a steady pulse called the beat.", 
                         "Fractions represent how long each note lasts.", 
                         "A whole note lasts the full beat."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Pulse of Time", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load assets
        metronome = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/metronome.svg")
        drumstick = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drumstick.svg")
        
        # Visual Elements
        anchor_point = Dot(color=WHITE)
        label_T = Text("Pulse", color=WHITE, font_size=20).next_to(anchor_point, UP)
        content_group = VGroup(anchor_point, label_T, metronome)
        
        self.place_at_grid(content_group, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        pulse_line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#FFD700").next_to(metronome, RIGHT)
        self.play(FadeIn(content_group), Create(pulse_line))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        whole_note = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00CED1", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(whole_note, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        half_line = Line(whole_note.get_left(), whole_note.get_right(), color="#00CED1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(whole_note), Create(half_line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        quarter_note = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FF6347", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(quarter_note, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(drumstick, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(quarter_note), FadeIn(drumstick))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF6347")
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Notes fill measures like water in a vessel.", "Each note occupies specific rhythmic space.", "They must sum to the measure's total capacity."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Measure Theory", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        robot = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg").set_color(WHITE)

        # Place animation center
        anim_group = VGroup(robot, block)
        self.place_at_grid(anim_group, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#1E90FF")

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADFF2F")

        final_block = block.copy().set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(FadeIn(final_block.next_to(block2, RIGHT)))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Dynamic Application: Changing Meters", [
            "Different time signatures change the musical feel.",
            "A 4/4 march feels structured and heavy.",
            "A 3/4 waltz spins in a circle."
        ])
        
        # Load asset
        character = ImageMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/character.png")
        
        # Elements for March and Waltz
        # B035: Offsetting animation vertical center (Row B/E)
        march_track = Square(side_length=2, color="#FF6347")
        waltz_track = RegularPolygon(n=3, radius=1.2, color="#9370DB")
        
        # Labels
        label_44 = Text("4/4 March", font_size=20, color="#FF6347")
        label_34 = Text("3/4 Waltz", font_size=20, color="#9370DB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF6347")
        # B002: Columns 4-6. B035: Row B for vertical offset.
        self.place_at_grid(march_track, "B4", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(character, "B4", scale_factor=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(label_44, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(march_track), FadeIn(character), Write(label_44))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#9370DB")
        # B035: Row E for vertical offset.
        self.place_at_grid(waltz_track, "E4", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(label_34, "F4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Morphing: The character stays centered as per requirement
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(march_track, waltz_track),
            FadeOut(label_44),
            Write(label_34),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", [
            "Beat is the unit of time.",
            "Measure is the container for notes.",
            "Time signature sets the rhythmic rule."
        ])

        # Assets
        container_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/container.svg", color=WHITE)
        ruler_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg", color=WHITE)
        metronome_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/metronome.svg", color=WHITE)

        # Objects
        beat_label = Text("Beat=Unit", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        beat_group = VGroup(beat_label)
        
        measure_label = Text("Measure=Container", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        measure_group = VGroup(measure_label, container_icon)
        container_icon.next_to(measure_label, UP)
        
        rule_label = Text("Rule=Signature", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        rule_group = VGroup(rule_label, ruler_icon)
        ruler_icon.next_to(rule_label, UP)

        # Sine wave
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4*PI], y_range=[-1, 1], axis_config={"include_ticks": False}).scale(0.5)
        sine = axes.plot(np.sin, color="#00CED1")
        wave_group = VGroup(sine, metronome_icon)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(beat_group, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(beat_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(measure_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(measure_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(rule_group, "D4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(rule_group))
        
        # Sine wave and metronome
        self.place_at_grid(wave_group, "E5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(sine), FadeIn(metronome_icon))
        self.play(Indicate(rule_group))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Rhythm of Mathematics: Understanding Music and Measure Theory
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in music theory and STEM

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Pulse of Time
sections.content: Define 'Beat' as the fundamental unit of time. Introduce the concept of a 'Fraction' as the mathematical basis for musical duration (Whole, Half, Quarter, Eighth notes).
sections.example: A mechanical owl's steady 'tick-tock' representing the constant beat, while its wings represent fractions of that time (1 full wing flap = 1 beat, half-flap = 1/2 beat).

sections.title: Defining the Measure (The Container)
sections.content: Explain that music is organized into 'Measures' (or bars) using Time Signatures. Introduce the Time Signature as a fraction where the numerator is beats per measure and the denominator is the note value that equals one beat.
sections.example: A visual animation of a 'Musical Basket' that can only hold a sum of 4/4 beats. If the basket is full, a wall appears, forcing the next notes into a new basket (measure).

sections.title: Visualizing Measure Theory
sections.content: Apply graphic representations to show how notes fill a measure like water filling a vessel. Use a stacked bar graph to demonstrate that different note lengths must sum up to the total capacity defined by the time signature.
sections.example: An animation of a robot composer placing blocks of different lengths into a slot; the blocks must equal exactly 4 units wide to fit perfectly into the '4/4 measure frame'.

sections.title: Dynamic Application: Changing Meters
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate how changing the time signature changes the 'gravity' or the feeling of the music. Contrast 4/4 (march) with 3/4 (waltz) using geometric shapes.
sections.example: A bouncy character jumping on tiles: in 4/4, they land on tiles 1 and 3 (heavy); in 3/4, they land on a triangle path, creating a circular, spinning rhythm.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Review: Beat = Unit, Measure = Container, Time Signature = Rule. Connect musical measures to periodic functions in mathematics.
sections.example: A final visual showing a Sine Wave overlaying a musical staff, where the peaks of the wave align perfectly with the start of every measure.
